title: Dev flow v2 result — native harness entry point
$comment: A SELF-CONTAINED composition of result.envelope.schema.json plus the four result.<role>.schema.json payload shapes, for a harness with its own native JSON-Schema validator (Workflow/Agent `schema`) that cannot run scripts/validate-result-schemas.mjs's role dispatch. `payload` is dispatched by role via `allOf` (one {if, then} pair per role — `if` matches `role`, `then` points `payload` at that role's `$defs` entry). The envelope-level `properties` (every key but `payload`, which stays the untyped {type: object} both files already agree on) and `required` above are copied VERBATIM from result.envelope.schema.json, and `$defs.implementer` / `$defs.challenger` / `$defs.reviewer` / `$defs.integrator` are their standalone schema files' bodies inlined VERBATIM too (same type/additionalProperties/required/properties/$defs/if/then), minus only $schema/$id/title/$comment, which make no sense on a $defs entry — scripts/test-result-schemas.sh asserts both equalities directly so neither representation can silently drift apart from its source. The one necessary edit anywhere in this file is `$defs.reviewer`'s and `$defs.challenger`'s own internal references: each standalone file's `#/$defs/finding` (and, for challenger, `#/$defs/attackScenario`) becomes `#/$defs/reviewer/$defs/finding` or `#/$defs/challenger/$defs/finding` (`#/$defs/challenger/$defs/attackScenario`) here, since those definitions now live nested under this file's own `$defs.<role>` rather than at that file's own root — the equality test normalizes exactly this one rewrite before comparing, and nothing else. Four more `allOf` members enforce status-conditional payload shape: the implementer completed/blocked REQUIREDNESS AND non-emptiness (payload.summary/handoff/ac_test_map present AND minLength/minItems-non-empty when role=implementer and status=completed; payload.blocked_question present AND non-empty when blocked), and the challenger completed/blocked `attack_scenarios` cardinality (minItems:1 when role=challenger and status=completed; maxItems:0 when blocked) — this is expressible HERE, unlike in the standalone result.implementer.schema.json / result.challenger.schema.json, precisely because `role` and `status` are both envelope-level fields this composed document can see in the same `if` as the `payload` property its `then` reaches into; each standalone payload-only schema never sees `status` at all, so ITS OWN property definitions stay unconditional — Foreman v1 serializes implementer's summary as `""` on a BLOCKED result, a shape the shared, unconditional property definition must still accept; only the status-conditional `then` branches here may narrow either role's fields further, and only for the completed/blocked case each actually applies to. Every OTHER receipt-validation semantic check (head agreement, run matching, id/pass/adjudication cross-checks, every integrator cross-field rule, challenger's attack_scenarios/findings cross-reference) still needs context or sibling fields no single schema-keyword condition can express; scripts/validate-result-schemas.mjs's checkImplementerStatus, checkChallengerAttackScenarios, and friends add all of it on top for any harness that can run them. See ai/schemas/README.md 'Native harness composition (result.schema.json)'. result.envelope.schema.json stays the deliberately envelope-only shape (payload: {type: object}, no dispatch) for whichever purpose only needs to validate the envelope fields themselves.

schema.$comment: Dev flow v2's envelope generation. Foreman v1's flat result.json used schema:1; v2 wraps the same fields (plus new envelope metadata) and bumps to 2.

role.description: Which role produced this result -- selects the payload schema (result.<role>.schema.json). The orchestrator is not a role that returns a result: it authors adjudication.schema.json and run.schema.json documents directly, never through this envelope.

status.description: completed: the role produced its full payload. blocked: the role could not (e.g. an implementer escalating a genuinely ambiguous spec per Foreman's v1 contract, or a finder that failed and will be retried once). See result.implementer.schema.json for the completed/blocked conditional fields it enforces via a receipt-validation semantic check, not a structural keyword, because the deciding field (this one) lives on the envelope while the conditioned fields live in payload.

head.description: The full commit SHA this result is about. Every head-shaped field elsewhere in a payload (reviewer's reviewed_head, integrator's codex_cycle.head and accepted.reviewed_commit) must equal this one -- enforced by the validator's receipt-validation pass, never by the payload schema alone, since the payload schema cannot see its sibling envelope field.

harness.description: e.g. claude-code, codex-cli. Free string -- the harness/model catalog is agent-registry.json's concern (#635), not this schema's.

tier.description: The tier the harness actually ran at. 'adaptive' is a config selector (.devflow.toml [role.*]), never an executed fact, so it is not a valid value here.

run.description: Immutable run identity only -- nothing mutable lives here. Mutable run state (stage transitions, interventions, outcome, pr) lives solely in run.schema.json, so an envelope and the run record can never disagree about it. Receipt validation rejects a run whose run_id/initiated_by are not those of the run the branch pointer currently names.

allOf.$comment: Same reasoning as the implementer completed/blocked pair above: role and status are both envelope-level fields this composed document can see in the same if as the payload property its then reaches into, which the standalone result.challenger.schema.json (payload-only, never sees status) cannot express. attack_scenarios minItems:1 already exists on the shared property; maxItems:0 for the blocked direction is why this schema-subset engine gained maxItems.

Challenger's completed/blocked attack_scenarios conditional, expressible here for the same reason as implementer's completed/blocked pair above: role and status are both envelope-level fields this composed document can see in the same if as the payload property its then reaches into. The standalone result.challenger.schema.json never sees status at all, so scripts/validate-result-schemas.mjs's checkChallengerAttackScenarios still enforces the identical rule for the standalone challenger kind, which never sees this composed schema.

summary.description: Required (non-empty) when the envelope's status is completed; ignored when blocked. No minLength here: Foreman v1 serializes this as "" (empty string, not absent) on a blocked result, so the schema must accept that shape. Enforced by the validator, not by this schema — checkImplementerStatus rejects an empty string on a completed result exactly as it would a missing one.

handoff.description: Required (non-empty) when the envelope's status is completed; ignored when blocked. No minLength here: Foreman v1 serializes this as "" (empty string, not absent) on a blocked result, so the schema must accept that shape. Enforced by the validator, not by this schema — checkImplementerStatus rejects an empty string on a completed result exactly as it would a missing one.

ac_test_map.description: Required (non-empty) when the envelope's status is completed; ignored when blocked. Each entry's own shape (criterion + a non-empty tests[]) is enforced structurally regardless of status, since v1 never permitted a malformed entry either way — only the requiredness of the whole array is status-conditional.

human_tasks.description: Optional at every status, exactly as in v1: Foreman's read_result() does data.get('human_tasks', []), so a v1 blocked result in particular can carry only schema/status/blocked_question with no human_tasks key at all. When present, still constrained to an array of strings.

blocked_question.description: Required (non-null) when blocked; ignored when completed. Enforced by the validator, not by this schema.

proposed_pr_title.description: Optional at every status, exactly as in v1.

stage.description: Always challenge — the challenger role never produces a review-stage pass (that is the reviewer role's contract, result.reviewer.schema.json). A single legal value is expressed as const, not a one-member enum, matching this family's convention for fields with exactly one valid value (e.g. the envelope's `schema: const 2`).

round.description: This pass's round number within the challenge stage, 1-based. Rounds are numbered independently per stage — see docs/product/domain.md 'A fix round returns to the stage that produced the findings; challenge and review keep separate round counts and caps.'

reviewed_head.description: Must equal the envelope's `head` — enforced by the validator's receipt-validation pass (schemas cannot see sibling fields outside their own instance).

finder.description: The external review product that produced this pass (e.g. codex-adversarial). Free string here — the finder catalog and its stage affinity are agent-registry.json's concern (#635), not this schema's. Must match the finder segment embedded in every finding id below (checked by the validator, not this schema).

findings.description: May be empty — a challenge round returning zero findings is a normal, schema-valid pass (specs/dev-flow-v2.md Acceptance criteria: a confidence role cannot end a stage on its own recommendation, including an empty findings list). A design-level finding is one with `class: design`; a de-scaffolding recommendation is one whose `recommended_disposition` is `delete` or `restructure` — both are ordinary entries in this same array, not a separate field.

counts.description: Per-priority finding counts for this pass. The validator cross-checks these against the actual `findings` tally.

attack_scenarios.description: Adversarial scenarios this pass attempted against the design or approach, independent of whether each one surfaced a finding — the record that the challenger actually attacked the change rather than only reporting what it happened to notice. Required non-empty when the envelope status is completed (a clean pass still records what it attempted) and required empty when blocked (scripts/validate-result-schemas.mjs's checkChallengerAttackScenarios). A scenario whose outcome is `surfaced-finding` names the finding it produced via `finding_id`; the validator cross-checks that id against this same pass's own `findings[]` (a same-document check, no external context needed).

id.description: Unique within the run by construction: <stage>-r<round>-<finder>-<n>. The validator checks the stage/round/finder segments match this pass's own stage/round/finder, and (given prior-run context) that the id collides with neither an earlier finding in this pass nor any finding already in the run.

path.description: Repo-relative path the finding is about.

line.description: 1-based line number, or null when the finding is not line-bound (e.g. a whole-file or cross-file design finding — the challenger's own contract, so this is common here). Design decision: null rather than 0 or omission, so 'not line-bound' is an explicit, typed value instead of a sentinel integer or an absent key a consumer could forget to check for.

provenance.description: original: about the change under review. round:N: about round N's fix, where N is a round of THIS SAME STAGE (challenge's round:N never refers to a review round). Asserted by the challenger; the exit script (#636) verifies it against the diff and may downgrade original to round:N with recorded evidence, never the reverse.

fingerprint.description: new: not seen before. repeat-of:<id> / supersedes:<id>: this finding is the same defect recurring, or a stronger restatement of an earlier one, where <id> is an earlier finding id in this run. Asserted by the challenger (which has prior rounds' findings in its brief); the exit script (#636) verifies it.

priority.description: The challenger's own label. The orchestrator's adjudicated priority (which may differ) lives in adjudication.schema.json, never here.

recommended_disposition.description: The challenger's recommendation only — never binding. `delete` and `restructure` are the two de-scaffolding recommendations (AGENTS.md 'Deleting the added code is a legitimate way to converge' / 'Restructuring to invariants'); the orchestrator's actual disposition lives in adjudication.schema.json.

id.description: Unique within this pass. Free-form (e.g. as-1) — unlike a finding id, an attack scenario is never adjudicated or cross-referenced from another document, so it carries no run-wide grammar.

description.description: What was attempted (the attack, failure scenario, or de-scaffolding angle explored).

outcome.description: held: the design withstood this scenario — no finding resulted. surfaced-finding: this scenario produced a finding, named by finding_id.

finding_id.description: Required key at every outcome; null when outcome is held (nothing to name), and a finding id from this same pass's findings[] when outcome is surfaced-finding — enforced by the if/then below and, for same-pass membership, by the validator (checkChallengerAttackScenarios).

round.description: This pass's round number within its stage, 1-based. Rounds are numbered independently per stage (challenge and review each start at 1) — see docs/product/domain.md 'A fix round returns to the stage that produced the findings; challenge and review keep separate round counts and caps.'

reviewed_head.description: Must equal the envelope's `head` — enforced by the validator's receipt-validation pass (schemas cannot see sibling fields outside their own instance).

finder.description: The external review product that produced this pass (e.g. codex-cli, codex-cloud, coderabbit, copilot). Free string here — the finder catalog and its stage affinity are agent-registry.json's concern (#635), not this schema's. Must match the finder segment embedded in every finding id below (checked by the validator, not this schema).

findings.description: May be empty — 'a reviewer round returns zero findings' is a normal, schema-valid pass (see specs/dev-flow-v2.md Acceptance criteria: a reviewer cannot end a stage — the reviewer's own recommendation, including an empty findings list, never decides the exit on its own).

counts.description: Per-priority finding counts for this pass. The validator cross-checks these against the actual `findings` tally.

id.description: Unique within the run by construction: <stage>-r<round>-<finder>-<n>. The validator checks the stage/round/finder segments match this pass's own stage/round/finder, and (given prior-run context) that the id collides with neither an earlier finding in this pass nor any finding already in the run. The stage word also admits `integration` (result.integrator.schema.json's findings[].id grammar), so a repeat-of/supersedes reference below can name an integration-stage finding — a reviewer pass's own stage/round/finder cross-check still confines its OWN id to challenge/review, since payload.stage itself has no integration value.

path.description: Repo-relative path the finding is about.

line.description: 1-based line number, or null when the finding is not line-bound (e.g. a whole-file or cross-file design finding). Design decision: null rather than 0 or omission, so 'not line-bound' is an explicit, typed value instead of a sentinel integer or an absent key a consumer could forget to check for.

provenance.description: original: about the change under review. round:N: about round N's fix, where N is a round of THIS SAME STAGE (challenge's round:N never refers to a review round and vice versa — provenance feeds per-stage divergence predicates in specs/dev-flow-v2.md § Convergence model v0, which are explicitly scoped per stage). Asserted by the reviewer; the exit script (#636) verifies it against the diff and may downgrade original to round:N with recorded evidence, never the reverse.

fingerprint.description: new: not seen before. repeat-of:<id> / supersedes:<id>: this finding is the same defect recurring, or a stronger restatement of an earlier one, where <id> is an earlier finding id in this run. Asserted by the reviewer (which has prior rounds' findings in its brief); the exit script (#636) verifies it.

priority.description: The reviewer's own label. The orchestrator's adjudicated priority (which may differ) lives in adjudication.schema.json, never here.

recommended_disposition.description: The reviewer's recommendation only — never binding. The orchestrator's actual disposition lives in adjudication.schema.json.

allOf.$comment: verdict: findings is a claim that something was actually surfaced — an empty findings array with that verdict is a contradiction (there is nothing to adjudicate). A second, independent {if, then} member, since this engine's if/then is a single conditional per schema node; allOf is how a second one composes alongside the verdict:clean one above.

checks.description: One entry per CI check gh pr checks reports.

bucket.description: gh pr checks --json bucket's own categorization of state: pass, fail, pending, skipping, or cancel.

run_id.description: The CI run identifier backing this check, as a string (GitHub ids are strings throughout this schema family except run.schema.json's author_actor_id — see ai/schemas/README.md).

required.description: Whether this is a required check (gh pr checks --required). A clean verdict demands bucket pass specifically from every required check; a non-required check may additionally be skipping (see checkIntegratorCleanVerdict) — an advisory check that never ran is not what blocks a clean read.

codex_cycle.description: null when the resolved integration cap is 0 (per specs/dev-flow-v2.md § Configuration, 'integration = 0 means no Codex cycle required') — the readiness gate's Codex-verdict condition drops out identically. Otherwise the current-head cycle this integrator run drove.

head.description: Must equal the envelope's `head` — enforced by the validator's receipt-validation pass.

cycle.description: The run-wide Codex cycle ordinal, counted against the resolved [caps].integration cap — increases with every new current-head Codex cycle this run drives (a fresh captured head, not a retry of the same one). Distinct from `attempt`: `cycle` counts CYCLES across the whole run, `attempt` counts RETRIES within one cycle's own captured head. Also distinct from the sibling `integration_round` (one level up, on the payload itself): `cycle` is null whenever `codex_cycle` itself is null (no Codex cycle ran this pass), so it is never what an integration finding id's round segment or an adjudication's `round` are checked against — see `integration_round`'s own description.

attempt.description: AGENTS.md's shepherd stage allows exactly two attempts per captured head before an incomplete cycle escalates. Distinct from `cycle` — see its description.

accepted.description: Present only when the cycle reached a terminal, non-escalated result (exit_code 0 or 10) — absent for exit codes 2/11/12/13/14, where no accepted evidence exists yet.

reviewed_commit.description: Must equal the envelope's `head` — enforced by the validator's receipt-validation pass, exactly like `head` above (this is the second, GitHub-side stamp of the same invariant).

exit_code.description: The verbatim exit code from ai/skills/universal/shepherd/assets/check-codex-cloud-review.sh's `check` subcommand: 0 clean, 10 findings, 11 pending, 12 retry, 13 escalate, 14 PR no longer open, 2 indeterminate.

integration_round.description: The run-wide ordinal of THIS integrator pass — independent of whether a Codex cycle ran (codex_cycle is null exactly when the resolved integration cap is 0, but a pass still happens and still needs an ordinal). This is what an integration finding id's own round segment and an integration-stage adjudication's `round` are checked against (checkIntegratorFindingIds, checkAdjudicationAgainstPass) — never `codex_cycle.cycle`, which counts Codex cycles specifically and is absent whenever codex_cycle itself is null, nor `codex_cycle.attempt`, which counts retries within one cycle's own captured head. Three different counters: integration_round counts passes, cycle counts Codex cycles, attempt counts retries per head.

findings.description: Findings surfaced during integration (human review comments, CI failures needing adjudication, an unsettled Codex finding) carried verbatim for the orchestrator to adjudicate — id, body, and source_id only, since the integrator never authors or interprets finding text. `id` follows the SAME finding-id grammar as a reviewer pass, with stage fixed to `integration`: integration-r<round>-<finder>-<n>, where round is the sibling `integration_round` and finder is the registry finder slug or `human` — this is what gives an integration finding an adjudication path through adjudication.schema.json exactly like a reviewer finding. `source_id` carries what `id` held before this schema adopted that grammar: the GitHub-native identifier of whatever surfaced the finding (an inline review comment id, a review id, a locally-minted marker for a CI failure).

id.description: integration-r<round>-<finder>-<n> — see the findings[] description above.

source_id.description: The GitHub-native id of the surfacing comment, review, or check — what `id` held before integrator findings adopted the shared finding-id grammar.

unanswered_thread_roots.description: Ids of inline review comment threads still missing their required per-thread reply.

settled_at.description: When this integrator pass was produced.

verdict.description: clean: nothing outstanding (checks green, Codex cycle terminal-clean or its findings settled, every thread answered) — applied_dispositions is required (may be empty if nothing needed fixing to reach this state). findings: something surfaced still needs orchestrator adjudication. pending: still waiting on CI or a reviewer — waiting is never a round (AGENTS.md), so re-dispatching the integrator for another look is normal. escalate: the remediation cap was reached with something unresolved.

applied_dispositions.description: What was applied to reach the current verdict (empty array if nothing needed disposing). Required whenever verdict is clean; optional otherwise — enforced above via if/then, since both fields live in this same payload.
